about.title: Pacifica Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and for families in Pacifica, that loss often comes without warning on a stretch of Cabrillo Highway or Sharp Park Road. San Mateo County records show 2 traffic deaths in the most recent final crash year, alongside 80 injury collisions and 106 people hurt — numbers that represent real households now facing funeral costs, lost income, and an absence no bill can measure. California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with certain dependents and heirs eligible if none of those survivors exist. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free service that connects grieving families with an independent, contingency-based attorney who can explain standing, deadlines, and what compensation may be available. You focus on your family. Let us help you find someone who can focus on the legal path forward, at no upfront cost.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to specific people — typically a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible afterward. An independent attorney can help sort out who has the right to bring a claim in your specific family situation.

items.title: Watching the Clock
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, but that window shrinks considerably if a government entity was involved, such as a claim tied to a public roadway. Acting sooner rather than later protects your family's options.

items.title: Recovering More Than Bills
items.desc: California law recognizes that wrongful death losses go beyond funeral costs and lost income to include the loss of love, companionship, and guidance a family member provided. An attorney can help make sure all of these losses are properly documented and presented.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives the surviving spouse, domestic partner, and children the first right to file. If none of those survivors exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible instead. An independent attorney can review your family's circumstances and confirm who qualifies.

items.question: Does a wrongful death claim relate to a criminal case if one is filed?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal charges that may arise from the same crash. The civil case focuses on compensating the family, while a criminal case, if pursued, addresses punishment. The two can move on different timelines and don't depend on each other.

items.question: Our loved one died in a crash near Sharp Park Road — does the location affect our claim?
items.answer: The location itself doesn't change your family's legal rights, but details like road conditions or signage near corridors such as Sharp Park Road or Highway 1 can sometimes matter to how a claim is evaluated. If a government entity's roadway design or maintenance is involved, shorter filing deadlines may apply. An attorney can look at the specific circumstances of the crash to advise you.

items.question: What kinds of compensation can a wrongful death claim cover?
items.answer: Recoverable losses in California typically include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Every family's situation is different, so an attorney can walk through what may apply to yours specifically.
